citation: National Laboratory of the Rockies. ResStock. https://resstock.nlr.gov/
description: ResStock is the U.S. Department of Energy's model of the residential building stock, developed and maintained by the National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL). It samples representative dwellings from a housing stock characteristics database of probability distributions and simulates each with physics-based OpenStudio and EnergyPlus models on high-performance computers, so that states, municipalities, utilities and manufacturers can see which upgrades save the most energy and money. Coverage is the United States circa 2018, now including Alaska and Hawaii, with annual and 15-minute results for weather years 2012 and 2018; the 2025 Release 1 datasets (October and November 2025) include 28 measure packages with electric vehicles, demand flexibility and electric panel estimates. Access: published datasets, an online data viewer, and open source code with its input distributions on GitHub. Licence: the code is under a BSD-style licence; datasets are free. Caveats: results are statistical representations, not models of real addresses; the March 2024 release computed bills incorrectly, as its page warns. Simulation uses are stock-level capacity planning of electrification, retrofit optimisation and climate scenarios. Related records: ComStock (commercial counterpart), End-Use Load Profiles for the U.S. Building Stock (dataset calibrated with it), OpenStudio and EnergyPlus.
